_meta.description: Master district/operator registry for the RECA yearbook-registry project. One entry per district that operates (or historically operated) schools in schools_master.json, plus districts discovered through Track C consolidation research.
conventions: successor_district_id: 'none' = still operating / no successor; 'unknown' = unresolved
predecessor_districts lists districts that merged INTO this district (and were dissolved by it)
types: public | parish_system | private_operator | county_special | state_agency | higher_ed

districts.name: Hazelwood School District

citations.note: US v. Hazelwood SD, 392 F.Supp. 1276: formed from thirteen rural school districts between 1949 and 1951 by annexation; 8 schools, 811 students at formation
District's own history page
PRiME Center (SLU): created as Hazelwood R-1 by the October 1951 reorganization vote

districts.notes: R-1 reorganization district created by the October 1951 county-wide vote; assembled from thirteen rural districts of St. Ferdinand Township (1949-1951 annexations). Covers 78 sq mi of northernmost St. Louis County.

districts.name: Ferguson-Florissant School District

citations.note: 1952 merger of Ferguson Public School District and Florissant School District
June 7, 1975 federal order annexing Berkeley and Kinloch districts into FFSD
515 F.2d 1365 (8th Cir. 1975) affirming annexation of Berkeley and Kinloch

districts.notes: Ferguson Reorganized School District R-2 created by the October 1951 reorganization vote, effecting the 1952 merger of the Ferguson and Florissant districts. Boundaries expanded effective February 1, 1975 to include the dissolved Berkeley and Kinloch districts under federal court order (388 F.Supp. 1058). Student desegregation implemented 1976-77 school year.

districts.name: Pattonville R-III School District

citations.note: Pattonville R-3 created by October 1951 reorganization vote
District history documenting the absorbed predecessor districts (Maryland Heights 1962, Bridgeton, Mount Pleasant, Penn-Junction, Fee Fee, St. Ann)

districts.notes: R-3 reorganization district from the October 1951 vote, built on the pre-existing School District of Pattonville; absorbed Bridgeton (~1950), Mount Pleasant and Penn-Junction (~1951), St. Ann, and Maryland Heights School District (1962). Modern spelling R-III is the canonical form; seed/rows variants 'R-3' and 'Pattonville School District' normalized.

districts.name: Normandy Schools Collaborative

citations.note: Established July 2014 by the Missouri State Board of Education, formerly the Normandy School District
District site; 2019-20 EleMiddle (grades 1-8) reconfiguration

districts.notes: The Normandy School District (DIST-106 lineage) was renamed/reconstituted as Normandy Schools Collaborative in July 2014 under state supervision following loss of accreditation; absorbed the dissolved Wellston district in 2010. Operates schools under the EleMiddle model since 2019-20.

districts.name: Ritenour School District

citations.note: District's own history compendium; school lineage back to a rural district school of 1867

districts.notes: Ritenour Consolidated School District descends from an 1867 rural school district (per the district's 'Our First 132 Years' history, 132 years to ~1999). Never dissolved; absorbed local elementaries through internal reorganizations (notably the March 25, 1976 plan closing Home Heights, Midland, and New Overland).

districts.name: Riverview Gardens School District

citations.note: District/alumni history: Riverview Gardens formed from the Science Hill District #20 and Moline predecessor districts

districts.notes: North-county district assembled from the Science Hill District #20 and Moline predecessor districts; RGSD high school opened in the 1950s (1218 Shepley Dr). Formation year probable; see notes for the circa-1950 consolidation.

districts.name: School District of University City

citations.note: District site

districts.notes: Independent district serving University City; formation date not established in Track C research (long predates the 1949 reorganization wave).

districts.name: St. Louis Public Schools

citations.note: District organized 1838; absorbed the Baden local district when Baden was annexed to the city in 1876

districts.notes: The city district; annexed-town districts (e.g. Baden, 1876) folded in as the city grew.

districts.name: Parkway C-2 School District

citations.note: 1954: Fern Ridge, Mason Ridge C-2, and Weber districts formed the consolidated high-school district Parkway C-2

districts.notes: Last major district merger of the St. Louis County consolidation wave.

districts.name: Ferguson Public School District

citations.note: 1952 merger of Ferguson Public School District and Florissant School District into FFSD

districts.notes: Also styled 'Ferguson School District' / 'District #3'. Operated Ferguson High School (1939) on the January Estate.

districts.name: Florissant School District

citations.note: 1952 merger into Ferguson-Florissant

districts.notes: The Florissant public district merged with Ferguson in the 1952 R-2 reorganization.

districts.name: Berkeley School District

citations.note: 515 F.2d 1365: Kinloch No. 18 split in 1937 into white Berkeley district and Black new Kinloch district; Berkeley annexed to FFSD by the 1975 order
1975 federal-ordered merger of Berkeley and Kinloch into FFSD

districts.notes: Created in the 1937 split of Kinloch School District No. 18; absorbed Scudder (1960) and Robertson (~1964) along the way; dissolved into Ferguson-Florissant effective February 1, 1975.

districts.name: Kinloch School District

citations.note: 1937 split of Kinloch No. 18 produced the all-Black new Kinloch district; annexed to FFSD effective Feb 1, 1975

districts.notes: The all-Black district created by the 1937 split; underfunded and segregated by state action per the federal courts (363 F.Supp. 739; 388 F.Supp. 1058).

districts.name: Kinloch School District No. 18

citations.note: Prior to 1937 one district (Kinloch No. 18) covered present-day Kinloch and most of Berkeley; split into two districts in 1937

districts.notes: Predecessor of BOTH Berkeley and Kinloch (the 1937 split created two districts from one). successor_district_id 'unknown' because there are two successors; see DIST-103 and DIST-104.

districts.name: Normandy School District

citations.note: Normandy School District became Normandy Schools Collaborative July 2014; absorbed Wellston district 2010

districts.notes: Longstanding north-county district; the 2014 change to the Collaborative was a state-directed reconstitution of the same legal district (succession recorded as rename).

districts.name: Scudder School District

citations.note: Scudder district history; merged into Berkeley School District 1960

districts.notes: Served the Scudder Avenue area; a portion of its territory had already gone to Kinloch No. 18 in 1902-03. Remainder merged into Berkeley in 1960; students then bused into Berkeley schools.

districts.name: Robertson School District

citations.note: Robertson district dissolved ~1964; students bused to Berkeley School District schools

districts.notes: Robertson district folded into Berkeley about 1964; its schools (e.g. Robertson Elementary, Robertson High School) came under Berkeley and then FFSD in 1975.

districts.name: Maryland Heights School District

citations.note: Pattonville district history: Maryland Heights district merged into Pattonville R-III in 1962

districts.notes: Founded as Rural District 24; at the 1962 merger it operated Maryland Heights High School, Remington Elementary, and Carver Elementary (Carver was discontinued at the merger).

districts.name: Bridgeton School District

citations.note: Pattonville district history; Bridgeton district annexed into Pattonville during the 1949-50 school year

districts.notes: Incorporated by the legislature in 1864, covering Bridgeton and Bridgeton Commons; like other small north-county districts it tuitioned secondary students out rather than operating a high school.

districts.name: Mount Pleasant School District

citations.note: Absorbed into Pattonville R-III at the 1951 reorganization

districts.notes: Mount Pleasant district folded into Pattonville; its school continued as a Pattonville elementary until 1978.

districts.name: Penn-Junction School District

citations.note: Penn-Junction combined the Penn and Junction districts; absorbed into Pattonville about 1950

districts.notes: Joint district formed from the earlier Penn and Junction school districts; its school (Penn-Junction School) continued under Pattonville until 1982.

districts.name: Penn School District

citations.note: Predecessor component of the Penn-Junction district

districts.notes: Early common school district that combined with Junction to form Penn-Junction.

districts.name: Junction School District

citations.note: Predecessor component of the Penn-Junction district

districts.notes: Early common school district that combined with Penn to form Penn-Junction.

districts.name: Fee Fee District No. 16

citations.note: Fee Fee District No. 16 became part of the School District of Pattonville (after 1930)

districts.notes: Common district along Fee Fee Creek; merged into the School District of Pattonville about 1930.

districts.name: School District of Pattonville

citations.note: Predecessor consolidated district; became Pattonville R-3 in the 1951 reorganization

districts.notes: The pre-1951 Pattonville district built around the Fee Fee Road school lineage; absorbed Fee Fee No. 16 in 1930. Formation year is the district's own tradition (1848); probable.

districts.name: St. Ann School District

citations.note: St. Ann district folded into Pattonville R-III

districts.notes: St. Ann area district absorbed by Pattonville; its elementary continued under Pattonville until 1982. Exact merger year not documented online.

districts.name: Science Hill School District #20

citations.note: Alumni/district history: Science Hill #20 predecessor of Riverview Gardens

districts.notes: Predecessor component of Riverview Gardens School District (with Moline).

districts.name: Wellston School District

citations.note: 2010: the state ordered Normandy to absorb the struggling district of Wellston

districts.notes: Dissolved and annexed into the Normandy district in 2010 — the last change to the county district map.

districts.name: Melrose School District No. 57
districts.notes: Rural district noted in seed/master as 'later merged into a west-county district' — the receiving district is not documented online; kept unknown pending a human follow-up.

districts.name: Brown School District

citations.note: One of the thirteen rural districts annexed into Hazelwood 1949-1951

districts.notes: Rural district of St. Ferdinand Township; its school closed ~1950 at consolidation; namesake continuation is Brown Elementary (Hazelwood SD).

districts.name: Cold Water School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district; school closed 1954.

districts.name: Prigge-Larimore School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: St. Ferdinand Township rural district; the Prigge/Larimore school line continues as Larimore Elementary (Hazelwood SD).

districts.name: Hyatt School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district; school closed 1951.

districts.name: Elm Grove School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood
Elm Grove District No. 9 established 1852

districts.notes: Elm Grove District No. 9, established 1852; its landmark school building was moved to Brookes Park in the 1960s.

districts.name: Pea Ridge School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district; school closed 1951.

districts.name: Columbia Bottom School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district on the Columbia Bottoms; school closed 1951.

districts.name: Vossenkemper School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district; school closed 1951.

districts.name: Black Jack School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: Rural district; school closed 1951.

districts.name: Twillman School District

citations.note: Thirteen-district annexation into Hazelwood

districts.notes: St. Ferdinand Township rural district; the Twillman school continued under Hazelwood.

districts.name: Rosary School District

citations.note: Florissant Valley historical sources name Rosary among the Hazelwood predecessor districts

districts.notes: Named among the thirteen Hazelwood feeder districts in local historical accounts; no school row in the registry (not in the seed). District-level record only.

districts.name: Garrett School District

citations.note: Named among the Hazelwood predecessor districts

districts.notes: One of the thirteen Hazelwood feeder districts per local historical accounts; no corresponding seed row.

districts.name: Bonfils School District

citations.note: Named among the Hazelwood predecessor districts

districts.notes: One of the thirteen Hazelwood feeder districts per local historical accounts; no corresponding seed row.

districts.name: Baden School District

citations.note: Baden annexed to the City of St. Louis in 1876, folding its local district into SLPS

districts.notes: The town of Baden's local school district; absorbed by St. Louis Public Schools when Baden joined the city in 1876.

districts.name: Moline School District

citations.note: Moline predecessor district of Riverview Gardens

districts.notes: Predecessor component of Riverview Gardens School District (with Science Hill #20).

districts.name: Fern Ridge School District

citations.note: Fern Ridge + Mason Ridge C-2 + Weber voted to form Parkway C-2 in 1954

districts.notes: West-county constituent of Parkway C-2.

districts.name: Mason Ridge C-2 School District

citations.note: Constituent of Parkway C-2 (1954)

districts.notes: West-county constituent of Parkway C-2.

districts.name: Weber School District

citations.note: Constituent of Parkway C-2 (1954)

districts.notes: West-county constituent of Parkway C-2.

districts.name: Wentzville R-IV School District

citations.note: Current district; serves Wentzville, Lake St. Louis, and adjacent areas
Wentzville High School established 1896 as a 2-year high school; reorganized as a full 4-year high school in 1939

districts.notes: St. Charles County's western district; its high school dates to 1896. The district's own reorganization/formation year was not pinned down in Track C research — probable per the R-IV designation arising from the county reorganization era.

districts.name: Fort Zumwalt R-II School District

citations.note: District history: Central School District R-II formed by voter approval July 19, 1949, combining 12 small districts; district's high school opened 1960

districts.notes: The O'Fallon-area district. Formed as Central School District R-II (1949) and later renamed Fort Zumwalt R-II — the rename year is not documented online; recorded as a rename of the same legal district (see DIST-203).

districts.name: Central School District R-II

citations.note: Formation approved by voters July 19, 1949, combining 12 small districts under the 1947 reorganization law

districts.notes: Twelve small St. Charles County districts combined into Central R-II in 1949 — predecessor identity of today's Fort Zumwalt district. (Note: the state plan's 'reorganized district' suffix 'R-II' is coincidentally the same numeral the modern Fort Zumwalt district carries.)

districts.name: O'Fallon School District

citations.note: O'Fallon school built 1869 at Convent Park (St. Mary's Academy grounds), first teacher Julius Reichenstein; local district consolidated into Central R-II in 1949

districts.notes: The O'Fallon local district, folded into Central School District R-II in the 1949 consolidation.

districts.name: Francis Howell R-III School District

citations.note: Official district history: 'District named as Francis Howell School District of St. Charles County, Missouri (1966, March 15)'

districts.notes: Successor name of Consolidated School District No. 2 (organized May 8, 1915). The district's official timeline gives the March 15, 1966 naming; recorded here as the district's modern identity — a rename, not a new legal entity.

districts.name: Consolidated School District No. 2 of St. Charles County

citations.note: Organized May 8, 1915 from rural common school districts plus the Francis Howell Institute; named Francis Howell School District March 15, 1966

districts.notes: Formed from a band of rural common-school districts and the Howell family's Francis Howell Institute (1881). One of the earliest consolidations — predating the 1947 reorganization law by three decades.

districts.name: New Melle School District
districts.notes: New Melle local district; folded into the Francis Howell district around 1949 (per the schools_master operator annotations). Exact year probable.

districts.name: St. Charles County common school districts
districts.notes: Umbrella entry for the many one-room common districts (e.g. District No. 68) that variously consolidated into Francis Howell R-III, Central R-II (Fort Zumwalt), Wentzville R-IV, or Orchard Farm. Individual named districts get their own rows when documented.

districts.name: School District of Washington

citations.note: District site

districts.notes: Franklin County district serving Washington, MO; operates Washington High School (est. 1889 per seed documentation). Formation year not established in Track C.

districts.name: Special School District of St. Louis County

citations.note: SSD formed 1957 to serve students with disabilities across St. Louis County districts

districts.notes: Countywide special-education district (Ackerman School 1961, South Tech 1967, North Tech 1968, et al.); partner districts refer students for services.

districts.name: Missouri Division of Youth Services

citations.note: MO Dept. of Social Services — Division of Youth Services operates residential school facilities

districts.notes: State agency operating residential/juvenile school facilities; took over some city-run residential programs in 1986 (e.g. the Girls' Industrial Home lineage).

districts.name: Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County

citations.note: The Junior College District established 1962 operates St. Louis Community College

districts.notes: The legal district behind St. Louis Community College (Florissant Valley, Forest Park, Meramec, Wildwood campuses). Some master rows list 'St. Louis Community College' as operator — normalized to the district.

districts.name: St. Charles Community College District

citations.note: SCC established by voters in 1986; first classes 1987

districts.notes: St. Charles County's community-college district.

districts.name: Archdiocese of St. Louis

citations.note: Archdiocese of St. Louis school system; parishes operate schools under archdiocesan supervision

districts.notes: System-level operator for all Catholic parish schools in the registry. Individual parishes (St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert, Sacred Heart, etc.) appear in district_operator as 'X Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis'. Includes the All Saints Academy partnership (DIST-402) and Christ, Light of the Nations inter-parish school.

districts.name: All Saints Academy

citations.note: St. Louis Review: multi-campus academy opened 2018 under St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert, and (formerly) St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parishes; St. Rose campus closed 2023, academy wound down

districts.notes: Inter-parish school network in Florissant (Federation of Catholic Schools, Northeast Deanery). Multi-campus model dissolved 2023; campuses' successor treatment recorded on the school rows.

districts.name: Lutheran High School Association of St. Louis

citations.note: LAHE/LCMS association operating Lutheran High School North and Lutheran High School South

districts.notes: Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod high-school association formed 1946 (Lutheran High School opened 1946 in the former Concordia College building); operates LHSN (opened 1950s) and LHSS.

districts.name: Sisters of Loretto

citations.note: Sisters of Loretto founded 1812; opened Nerinx Hall 1924

districts.notes: Religious congregation operating Loretto Academy (1907-1952) and Nerinx Hall (1924-present) in Webster Groves.

districts.name: Lindenwood University

citations.note: Private university, St. Charles MO

districts.notes: Operated a Florissant 'North County Center' extension site in the former Our Lady of Fatima school building (2006-~2022).

districts.name: Saint Louis University

citations.note: Private Jesuit university

districts.notes: Operator of university-lab-school records in the registry (e.g. the College Farm/Most Holy Name of Jesus site on E. Grand Blvd).

districts.name: Washington University in St. Louis

citations.note: Private research university

districts.notes: Operator affiliation for university-associated school records in the registry.

districts.name: Sisters of Charity of the Incarnate Word
districts.notes: Religious congregation recorded as operator for a residential/institutional school row in the registry.

districts.name: Olivet University
districts.notes: Private religious university; operator of a school row in the registry.

districts.name: University of Missouri System

citations.note: University of Missouri system established 1963

districts.notes: Operator affiliation for UM-St. Louis associated records in the registry.
